items.stem: Why should builds run on Jenkins agents rather than on the controller?

options.text: To isolate workloads and keep the controller responsive and stable
options.rationale: Correct: agents isolate build work, protecting the controller's stability.

options.text: Because the controller cannot run any steps
options.rationale: It technically can, but doing so is discouraged.
Credentials live in the credentials store, not on agents by design.

options.text: Because declarative pipelines require it syntactically
options.rationale: Declarative syntax does not mandate the controller/agent choice.

items.explanation: Correct: agents isolate build work, protecting the controller's stability.

items.stem: Which practices improve Jenkins pipeline reliability? (Select TWO)

options.text: Adding timeouts to stages that could hang
options.rationale: Correct: timeouts stop a hung stage from blocking executors indefinitely.

options.text: Using a post block to clean up regardless of outcome
options.rationale: Correct: post{always} ensures cleanup even when a stage fails.

options.text: Echoing credentials into the build log for debugging
Marking the build successful even when tests fail
options.rationale: Hiding failures defeats the purpose of CI.

items.explanation: Correct: timeouts stop a hung stage from blocking executors indefinitely.; Correct: post{always} ensures cleanup even when a stage fails.

items.stem: What is the correct way to use a stored secret inside a Jenkins pipeline step?

options.text: Bind it with withCredentials so it is masked and scoped to the block
options.rationale: Correct: withCredentials injects the secret into a limited scope and masks it in logs.

options.text: Print it with echo to confirm the value
options.rationale: Printing a secret exposes it in the log.
Hard-coding secrets puts them in version control.

options.text: Store it as a plain environment variable in the repo
options.rationale: Plain repo variables are not a secure secret store.

items.explanation: Correct: withCredentials injects the secret into a limited scope and masks it in logs.
